title: Astrid and the Monsoon
premise: Orsen Eriksen, a bush pilot who delivers medicine and gossip to scattered coastal settlements, has spent years keeping their past buried and their heart locked. When a record-low monsoon tide exposes a sea cave holding the wreck of the Meridian Star—and a passenger manifest that names Orsen's vanished mother—the legends stop being stories and start being leverage. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet captain who has six tides to claim the wreck legally, Orsen must decide whether the truth of who they are is worth surrendering the invisibility that has kept them safe. In the end, Orsen reaches the wreck first but chooses to give the salvage rights to the coastal communities whose ancestors died aboard, finding belonging not in hiding but in standing among people who now know everything.
about_author: J. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent a decade ferrying supplies along remote coastlines before turning to fiction. Their work draws on tide tables, radio chatter, and the particular loneliness of people who live where the maps run out.

chapters.title: Weather Coming In
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A routine medicine run through worsening weather establishes Orsen's competence, isolation, and the rule they live by: land, deliver, leave, remember nothing. A radio warning about an approaching monsoon system plants dread. Emotional beat: the comfort and cost of being no one in particular.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Grounded by the storm at the fishing village of Salt Hollow, Orsen walks the emptied bay at extreme low tide and finds the cave mouth—black, breathing, impossible. Old-timer Marta recognizes it from legend and goes pale. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease as something long hidden surfaces.

chapters.title: What the Cave Kept
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with a flashback thread. Inside the cave at slack water, Orsen finds the ribs of a wrecked ship and a corroded plaque: Meridian Star, 1947. Among the debris, a locket Orsen recognizes from childhood photographs. Emotional beat: the past reaching up and taking hold.

chapters.title: Rumors Fly Faster Than Planes
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Word spreads through Salt Hollow's radio net before Orsen can decide what to do. The village splits between those who see fortune and those who fear outsiders. Emotional beat: Orsen realizes invisibility was always borrowed time, never a guarantee.

chapters.title: The Man from the Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Anton Reyes's POV. Captain Anton Reyes arrives on the survey vessel Corvus, waving a salvage permit and a six-tide deadline granted under maritime law. Charming, patient, and utterly certain he will win. Emotional beat: cold professionalism meeting warm resistance; the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen calculates the tides: the cave is accessible only at extreme lows, and only two more such lows fall within the legal window—both after Reyes's deadline. But Reyes has dynamite permits pending. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; Orsen decides to fight for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Missing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Researching in the village archive, Orsen confirms their mother, Ingrid Eriksen, was listed as a passenger on the Meridian Star—and officially listed among the dead. Orsen has spent a lifetime believing she abandoned them. Emotional beat: grief reopened; identity cracking open like the hull.

chapters.title: The Doctor Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Dr. Priya Nair's POV. Priya, the young physician Orsen has flown medicine to for three years, notices Orsen unraveling and refuses to let them carry it alone. A quiet scene over bad coffee becomes the first honest conversation Orsen has had in a decade. Emotional beat: love arriving unannounced, unwelcome, undeniable.

chapters.title: Dynamite and Due Process
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes secures his blasting permit by exploiting a jurisdictional loophole, revealing the political pressure behind his mission—a wealthy backer wants the Meridian Star's rumored gold. Emotional beat: the antagonist humanized but hardened; duty versus conscience begins echoing the book's central theme.

chapters.title: Low Water, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen dives the second chamber despite a storm-swollen current and finds the passenger compartment sealed since 1947—including evidence Ingrid survived the wreck and left deliberately, faking her death. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief tangled together; the mother was a coward or a survivor, maybe both.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Salt Hollow holds a storm-lantern meeting on the beach. Some want to sell information to Reyes; others want the wreck declared a communal grave site. Orsen, asked directly whose side they're on, hesitates—and the hesitation costs them trust. Emotional beat: belonging demanded, not given; Orsen's old strategy fails publicly.

chapters.title: Flight into the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen flies through the monsoon's leading edge to the regional records office to find Ingrid's trail, nearly dying when the engine ices. They return with a name: Ingrid lived under another identity until eight years ago—in the very region Reyes's backer comes from. Emotional beat: obsession threatening to consume everything else.

chapters.title: What Priya Saw
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Orsen about flying reckless, about disappearing into the mystery, about choosing a dead woman's secrets over living people. She admits her feelings and dares Orsen to admit theirs. Emotional beat: love against duty stated plainly; Orsen cannot yet answer.

chapters.title: The Corvus Moves
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. With the blasting permit signed, Reyes positions the Corvus over the cave for the next low tide. His crew includes a diver who once worked with Ingrid under her assumed name—and who quietly tells Reyes what he knows. Emotional beat: the antagonist gains leverage and a flicker of doubt.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Someone cuts the Corvus's mooring lines overnight. Orsen didn't do it—but every finger points their way, and the magistrate threatens to revoke what little standing the villagers have. Emotional beat: injustice closing in; Orsen learns how easily a community can turn on its own.

chapters.title: Confessions at Slack Tide
chapters.summary: Orsen and Priya dual POV. Trapped together in the cave by an early tide, Orsen tells Priya everything—the mother, the lies, the years of hiding. Priya answers with her own secret: she came to Salt Hollow fleeing a malpractice scandal. Emotional beat: mutual exposure; intimacy built from shared damage.

chapters.title: The Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes begins controlled demolition early, against his own better judgment, pressured by his backer's arrival on-site. The blast cracks the cave's inner chamber—and reveals not gold but a wall of personal effects, letters, and the truth that the 'treasure' legend was cover for a smuggling operation gone wrong. Emotional beat: victory turning hollow.

chapters.title: Letters from the Dead
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Among the exposed effects, Orsen finds Ingrid's final letter, written before she vanished: she stayed behind to shield a lover accused in the smuggling ring, then fled to protect her child from the fallout. Her disappearance was sacrifice, not abandonment. Emotional beat: catharsis; the wound reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Standing Ground
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the final low tide, with Reyes's crew moving to strip the chamber, Orsen lands the plane on the tidal flats and stands physically between the salvagers and the cave, backed by all of Salt Hollow. Reyes, confronted with the letters proving the dead were victims, not criminals, makes his choice. Emotional beat: courage as community; Orsen finally visible, finally claimed.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes voids his own contract, citing falsified provenance documents from his backer, and walks away from the richest find of his career. His backer threatens him; Reyes accepts the consequences. Emotional beat: the antagonist's redemption mirrors Orsen's arc—duty redefined as conscience.

chapters.title: What Belongs to the Sea
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The wreck is dedicated as a memorial; the effects are returned to descendants across the coast, including Orsen's own hands receiving Ingrid's letter formally, witnessed. Orsen scatters nothing and keeps everything—the truth, at last, held openly. Emotional beat: grief resolved into gratitude; identity integrated.

chapters.title: First Light, Full Tank
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Weeks later, Orsen preps the plane for the morning run, Priya's spare stethoscope on the passenger seat, Marta's bread in the cargo hold, the whole coast on the radio saying their name like it belongs there. Orsen takes off into clear post-monsoon light. Emotional beat: departure transformed—from escape into homecoming, every flight a return.
